Iron Age Europe had weaving combs of whalebone. From hairdressing, hair ornament, ritual and craft uses the comb developed a way of plucking teeth of unequal length, and this inspired the kazoo, the thumb piano and the music box.

梳子琴以葉片或紙張覆於梳齒一側，另一側以抿唇哼唱，可明顯增加人聲的高頻泛音，使頻: The comb is played by covering one side of the teeth with a leaf or paper and humming with pursed lips on the other side, which markedly increases the high overtones of the voice and spreads the spectrum; the timbre is modulated as the resonance frequency of the mouth cavity changes. The teeth themselves also carry overtones, whose character is set by their shape, length and material. Teeth of unequal length can be plucked to give different notes, and the range depends on how the teeth are laid out. Unlike membranophones such as the kazoo, its core sound source is still the humming and the resonance of the teeth; compared with the later thumb piano and music box, the comb is simpler in construction, and its change of pitch comes directly from the length of the teeth.

演奏梳子琴時，可將植物葉片或紙張蒙在梳子一側，嘴唇收攏後在另一側哼唱，使聲音經梳: To play the comb, stretch a plant leaf or paper over one side, purse the lips and hum against the other side, so that the sound passes the teeth and the covering and gains more high overtones; changing the resonance frequency of the mouth adjusts the spectrum. Another way is to pluck the teeth with a finger, which gives different notes when the teeth differ in length. A beginner can first pluck teeth of different lengths one by one, then practise the shape of the mouth together with the humming. Timbre and pitch depend on the shape, length and material of the teeth.
